desc: Designs and sells consumer and professional 3D printers, scanners and filaments under the Creality brand worldwide.
markets: Hobbyist and prosumer 3D-printing buyers in North America, Europe and Asia; sells online and through distributors abroad.
rationale: Additive manufacturing tie-in to F1 engineering; brand building with makers and tech enthusiasts in Europe and the Americas.
signals: Listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (2025)

desc: Makes sports nutrition, protein, supplements and energy drinks sold under the Applied Nutrition brand.
markets: UK core market with sales through retailers and distributors in Europe, the Middle East and other export markets.
rationale: Performance-nutrition positioning suits driver fitness content; UK and Middle East brand building around races.

desc: Develops and wholesales aluminium alloy wheels and car aftermarket accessories, including the WedsSport and Leonis brands.
markets: Mainly Japanese car aftermarket and tyre retailers; some exports. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Motorsport-linked wheel brand could use F1 imagery to support aftermarket sales in Japan and Asia.
sports: Sponsor of the WedsSport-branded Racing Project Bandoh team in Japan's Super GT

desc: Provides digital on-demand manufacturing: CNC machining, injection moulding, 3D printing and sheet-metal parts for engineers.
markets: Product developers and manufacturers in the US and Europe, with operations in Germany and a supplier network.
rationale: Rapid-prototyping showcase with engineering teams; B2B hospitality to reach product-development and procurement buyers.

desc: Designs and manufactures DC fast-charging systems for electric cars, buses, trucks and fleets.
markets: Nordic and European charge-point operators and fleets, expanding into North America with a US factory.
rationale: Showcase of electrification technology; B2B hospitality with fleet operators and charge-point operators in Europe and North America.

desc: Supplies automotive test systems, driving robots, driving simulators and simulation software to carmakers and motorsport teams.
markets: Carmakers, suppliers and test bodies in Europe, North America and Asia; simulation brands include rFpro and Ansible Motion.
rationale: Its simulators and simulation software sell to motorsport engineers; F1 visibility supports its technology credibility with OEMs.

desc: Develops luxury residential and branded real-estate projects in the Middle East, Europe and other international markets.
markets: Projects in Saudi Arabia, UAE, Oman, Qatar, Spain and the UK, aimed at wealthy international buyers.
rationale: Luxury-property marketing to wealthy buyers around Gulf races; a rival developer, DAMAC, already sponsors in F1.
flags: majority-owned subsidiary of Dar Al Arkan

desc: Operates and franchises Guzman y Gomez Mexican quick-service restaurants in Australia and other countries.
markets: Australia core, plus restaurants in Singapore, Japan and the United States, where it is expanding.
rationale: Brand building in Australia and the US through Melbourne, Miami, Austin and Las Vegas races.

desc: Provides car design, engineering and styling services, and licenses the Pininfarina brand for vehicles and products.
markets: Carmakers and industrial and architecture clients in Europe, Asia and the Middle East.
rationale: Italian automotive design heritage suits F1 luxury positioning; showcase for design services to carmakers.

desc: Makes and sells automotive and industrial lubricants in India, chiefly under the Veedol brand.
markets: Indian automotive and industrial lubricant market, with some exports. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Lubricant category is traditional in F1; rivals Castrol and Gulf use motorsport to sell to Indian motorists.

desc: Designs and sells PC cases, power supplies, cooling systems and gaming peripherals under the Thermaltake brand.
markets: PC builders and gamers in North America, Europe and Asia, sold through retailers and online channels.
rationale: Gaming and sim-racing audience overlaps with F1 fans; Thermaltake could target PC gamers in many race markets.

desc: Provides 3D-printing software, engineering services and printed parts for industrial and medical customers.
markets: Industrial and medical customers in Europe, the US and Asia; medical planning and personalised implants are a growing segment.
rationale: Additive manufacturing and software tie-in with F1 engineering; B2B hospitality for industrial and healthcare clients.

desc: Manufactures and markets Castrol automotive and industrial lubricants in India.
markets: Indian car, motorcycle, commercial-vehicle and industrial lubricant users. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Castrol is an established F1 lubricant brand; Indian activation could support motorcycle and car oil sales.
f1: Castrol (BP group) - listed on the current F1 partner roster
flags: majority-owned subsidiary of BP (Castrol); BP agreed in 2025 to sell a majority of Castrol to Stonepeak
signals: BP agreed to sell a 65% stake in Castrol to Stonepeak (December 2025)

desc: Makes portable power stations and solar generators sold internationally under the Jackery brand.
markets: Consumers in North America, Japan and Europe, sold through Amazon, retailers and its own websites.
rationale: Outdoor and backup-power brand building in the US, Japan and Europe; portable energy demonstrations at circuits and fan zones.

desc: Designs and sells action cameras, accessories and subscription software for capturing and editing video.
markets: Consumers in North America, Europe and Asia through retailers and online; subscription service worldwide.
rationale: Onboard and immersive racing footage suits its product; brand reach with young fans in race markets.

desc: Designs and manufactures LED video displays, scoreboards and digital signage for stadiums, venues and transport.
markets: Sports venues, advertisers and transport operators mainly in North America, plus Europe and Asia.
rationale: Circuit and fan-zone display supplier showcase; contacts with venue operators and promoters at US races.

desc: Makes polymer 3D printers, materials and software used for prototyping and production parts by manufacturers.
markets: Aerospace, automotive, medical and consumer-goods manufacturers in the Americas, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Additive manufacturing for race-car parts is a direct technology showcase; already on the F1 partner roster.
f1: Stratasys - on the current F1 partner roster (added 2026)

desc: Operates online FX, CFD, securities and crypto trading services for retail investors, mainly through GMO Click Securities.
markets: Japanese retail traders, with FX operations in Thailand and other Asian markets.
rationale: Online trading brokers such as eToro and Pepperstone use F1 for trader acquisition; Japan Grand Prix activation possible.
flags: majority-owned subsidiary of GMO Internet Group

desc: Makes live video production systems, replay servers and media software used by sports broadcasters worldwide.
markets: Broadcasters, production companies and leagues across Europe, the Americas, the Middle East and Asia.
rationale: Live replay and broadcast technology fits F1 production; hospitality for broadcaster and rights-holder customers.

desc: Designs and manufactures home, business and public chargers for electric vehicles, plus energy-management software.
markets: Europe core, with sales in North America, Latin America and Asia.
rationale: EV-charging brand building with car buyers in Europe and the Americas; technology showcase on electrification.

desc: Provides automotive software engineering for electric powertrains, autonomous driving, connected vehicles and software-defined cars.
markets: Carmakers and suppliers in Europe, the US and Asia, with operations in Germany, the US, Japan and China.
rationale: Automotive software and engineering tie-in with F1; hospitality for carmaker engineering buyers.

desc: Makes and markets Gulf-branded automotive and industrial lubricants in India.
markets: Indian motorcycle, car and commercial-vehicle lubricant market, plus some exports. No verified expansion plans.
rationale: Group brand Gulf is already in F1; Indian activation could support lubricant sales to motorists.
f1: Gulf Oil International (Hinduja group) - on the current F1 partner roster
flags: majority-owned subsidiary of Gulf Oil (Hinduja group)

desc: Designs and sells premium speakers, headphones and televisions under the Bang & Olufsen brand.
markets: Wealthy consumers in Europe, the US, China and Asia through own stores and partners.
rationale: Luxury audio brand fits F1's premium audience; hospitality and product placement in Europe, Asia and the Middle East.

desc: Sells consumer health supplements under the IM8 brand, after moving away from genetic and diagnostic testing.
markets: Direct-to-consumer supplement buyers in the US, UK and Asia.
rationale: Health and longevity brand building with affluent consumers in the US and Asia.

desc: Designs and sells Bluetooth communication systems and smart helmets for motorcyclists and outdoor sports users.
markets: Motorcycle and outdoor-sports riders in North America, Europe and Asia; US subsidiary in California.
rationale: Motorsport-minded riders overlap with F1 fans; brand building in the US and Europe.

desc: Develops and licenses helmet safety technology to helmet brands for cycling, motorcycling, snow sports and work.
markets: Helmet brands sold in North America, Europe and Asia; expanding in motorcycle and safety helmets.
rationale: Head-protection technology fits motorsport safety messaging; brand awareness with helmet buyers.

desc: Designs and sells performance car parts, fuel systems and accessories for enthusiasts, under brands such as Holley.
markets: Mainly US car enthusiasts, with some international sales.
rationale: Performance-parts enthusiasts follow motorsport; the Miami, Austin and Las Vegas races offer US brand activation.
sports: Holley organises enthusiast events such as LS Fest

desc: Designs and sells gaming accessories, notably Thrustmaster racing wheels and Hercules audio products for DJs.
markets: Gamers and sim-racers in Europe, North America and Asia.
rationale: Thrustmaster racing wheels serve sim-racing fans; F1 esports and fan-zone activation fit well.

desc: Makes 3D printers, materials, software and on-demand parts for industrial, healthcare and dental customers.
markets: Healthcare, aerospace, automotive and industrial customers in the US, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Long-running F1 technical partnership showcases additive manufacturing for race-car parts.
f1: 3D Systems - technical partner of an F1 team (on the current F1 partner roster)

desc: Designs and sells gaming headsets, controllers and simulation accessories for consoles and PCs.
markets: Gamers in North America, Europe and Australia, through retailers and online.
rationale: Racing-sim accessories and headsets suit F1's gaming fans; brand building in the US and Europe.
